hints: Look separately at the steroid skeleton and the side chain, remembering that every vertex and every labelled group in skeletal formula hides a carbon.
Count all carbons first: the fused ring system plus its two angular methyl groups gives 19 carbons, then add the 4 carbons of the side chain.
Recall a chiral carbon is tetrahedral with four different groups, so rule out all $C=O$, $C=C$ and $CH_2$ carbons and check only $CH$ and quaternary carbons for four different attachments.
walkthrough:
**Count the carbon skeleton**

Steroids look scary, but just count carefully. The four fused rings contain 17 ring carbons.

Add the two angular $CH_3$ groups shown:
$$17 + 2 = 19 \text{ carbons in steroid core}$$

**Count the side-chain carbons**

Look at the top right group: $-C(=O)-CH_2-O-C(=O)-CH_3$. That is very easy to miss.

Count them:
$$1 (ketone) + 1 (CH_2) + 1 (ester C=O) + 1 (CH_3) = 4 \text{ carbons}$$ 
So total $C$ atoms $= 19 + 4 = 23$.

**Recall what makes a carbon chiral**

A chiral atom here means a tetrahedral $sp^3$ carbon with four different groups attached. This immediately rules out:
$$C=O, \text{ } C=C, \text{ } CH_2, \text{ } CH_3$$
Only $CH$ carbons and carbons joined to four other carbons can be chiral.

**Find the 7 chiral centres**

Work round the rings. Four $CH$ ring junctions and the $CH(OH)$ are all chiral, plus the two quaternary $C(CH_3)$ junctions and the tertiary alcohol $C(OH)$ on the five-membered ring.

That gives $5 + 2 = 7$ chiral carbons in total, so the correct row is 23 carbons and 7 chiral atoms.

options.A: 22 carbons is one too few. This usually happens if you miss one carbonyl carbon in the $-CO-CH_2-OCO-CH_3$ side chain. The chiral count of 7 is correct.
options.B: 22 carbons misses a side-chain carbon, and 8 chiral atoms is one too many. The extra chiral centre often comes from mistakenly counting a $CH_2$ or a $C=C$ carbon as chiral.
options.C: Correct. There are 19 carbons in the steroid nucleus with its two methyl groups plus 4 in the side chain, giving 23. Only 7 tetrahedral carbons have four different groups, all others are $C=O$, $C=C$, $CH_2$ or $CH_3$.
options.D: 23 carbons is correct, but 8 chiral atoms is one too many. This trap comes from counting an additional ring $CH_2$ or alkene carbon which cannot be chiral because it does not have four different single-bonded groups.
